newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns of possible bomb blasts in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns of possible bomb blasts in Nigeria.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said Tuesday it had received information that bomb attacks might take place at Nigerian airports during the last two weeks of December.
A public announcement did not say where the information came from, or provide further details.

"There is no indication of a threat directed against American citizens," the announcement said. "However, Americans in or travelling to Nigeria should exercise caution and report suspicious activity to the local police or the American embassy."
A Nigerian army colonel who is one of the closest aides of military ruler Gen. Sani Abacha narrowly escaped a bomb blast Monday and police said they did not rule out political motives for the attack.

Col. Muhammed Marwa, the military administrator of Lagos state, was not hurt but the explosion seriously injured two security men sitting in the last car of the convoy in which he was travelling as well as a civilian bystander.
Police said six people had been arrested but it was not clear who was behind the blast.
